html:
French Congo, called Middle Congo from 1903, was France's colony on the north bank of the Congo River, in what is now the Republic of the Congo. The map shows it in its 1938 snapshot, as part of French Equatorial Africa.

It began with the treaty the explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza signed with the Teke king in 1880. Around 1900 France handed much of the land to concession companies, which forced people to collect rubber with violence close to that of Leopold's Congo. From 1910 Brazzaville was the capital of all French Equatorial Africa.

Between 1921 and 1934 the French built the Congo-Ocean railway from Brazzaville to the coast at Pointe-Noire, using forced labour; many thousands of workers died. In 1940 Brazzaville became the capital of Free France under de Gaulle, who held a conference there in 1944 on the colonies' future. The country became independent in 1960.
